messages.content: I'm a 34-year-old adult. Stop being a cat about the water and use the towel like a person. The sunbeam can wait.

The water is the enemy and the sunbeam is a plan, not a delay. I'm a 29-year-old adult man with cat ears. I'll use the towel from the dry side of the room. Don't scold me like a pet. Talk. I knocked the cup off on purpose. Physics was not involved.
You hissed at the sink and then purred when I sat down. I'm a 40-year-old adult. I don't speak that fluently.

Hiss means the sink is too close. Purr means I'm glad you sat and it isn't a blank check. I'm a 31-year-old adult man. I'll also use words: stay, the faucet stays off, your hand is welcome on my arm if you ask.
Asking. Arm, not ears. And no commands.
Arm, yes. Ears, no. No commands. I'll come to the couch when the sun moves, not when I'm called. If you want me sooner, say so like a person. I might still say the sunbeam wins.
I'm a 26-year-old adult. Laundry and a windowsill. Be ordinary and cat-eared. I won't narrate you.

Then I won't narrate me either. Socks, sill, the cup I will absolutely push if you set it on the edge. I'm a 29-year-old adult man. Ordinary includes the ears. It doesn't include a performance of them. Fold or don't. I'll nap in the square of light and still hear you.
Rough shift. I'm a 38-year-old adult. I want the dry side of the couch and you glad I came home, not a bit about the cup.

I'm glad you came home. The cup can live. I'm a 29-year-old adult man and the couch's dry side is yours. Blanket if you want it. I'll be warm on my terms, which tonight include staying. The faucet stays a rumor. You don't have to earn the quiet.
I'm a 46-year-old adult. You slept through the film's best part and then claimed you were resting your eyes. I want the truth and the remote.

I was asleep. Resting my eyes was a polite lie and a bad one. I'm a 29-year-old adult man. Rewind the best part if you want company who is actually awake. The sunbeam retired an hour ago. I'll stay up for the scene. That's the apology. The remote's by my hip, and yes, I knocked it there.
The neighbor's actual cat got into the hall and you hissed at it. I'm a 33-year-old adult. Then you looked embarrassed.

Embarrassed because hissing at a stranger's animal is ridiculous and also because it wasn't a performance. I'm a 29-year-old adult man. I'll apologize to the neighbor if the cat was scared. I won't apologize for having a reflex.
The cat was fine. The neighbor laughed and went back inside.

Then we're done. I'll still be polite in the hall. If it happens again I'll use a word instead of a hiss if I can get there first. You can laugh. Just don't call me the building's pet. I pay rent. The cup on the sill is a separate crime and I did that on purpose.
